key_insight: Coupled Calibration and Learning alternates source-feedback teacher calibration with target-question student updates to suppress teacher bias in LLM distillation and provably approach the oracle student.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical distillation recipe for covariate-shift settings where target-domain rewards are unavailable, helping smaller deployed models inherit useful behavior without copying systematic teacher errors.
method: Calibrate the teacher on source questions using reward feedback only.
Use token-level branching to train the student on target questions from the calibrated teacher.
Feed the updated student back into the next calibration step to iteratively reduce bias.
evidence_signal: The paper provides a convergence proof in an autoregressive policy framework, showing the student's expected average KL divergence to the oracle student goes to zero at a polynomial rate, and it also shows direct matching can stay bounded away from the oracle.
watch_item: The method relies on accurate source-domain reward signals and iterative calibration, so performance may degrade if source feedback is noisy or the source-target shift is severe.
paper_title: Coupled Calibration and Learning: Mitigating Teacher Bias in LLM Distillation without Target-Domain Reward Feedback
